title: Synthetic Lab: Regression Harness for Toolcall Edgecases and Streaming Compatibility
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a deterministic, lightweight regression harness ("Synthetic Lab") that systematically validates combined streaming + function/tool-calling + structured-output behavior across runtime variants. The harness will generate corpus permutations (golden seeds, injected edgecases, and synthetic fuzzes), run them against a matrix of model/runtime configurations, and produce human-readable diffs and CI-friendly fingerprints. Goal: detect contract regressions earlier (off-main CI) and provide a canary suite that gates releases for API compatibility guarantees.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can execute a canonical workload of 200 golden seeds and 1200 synthetic permutations within an hour on CI runners
For each run the harness emits a compact fingerprint (hash) per test that is stable across identical runtime/model combos
CI pipeline integrates a gating job that fails on >0.5% contract regressions vs baseline for critical routes (chat/streaming/toolcall)
Regression reports include: failing test id, human-readable diff, request/response snapshot, and suggested remediation tags (flaky, schema-drift, performance)
implementation_steps: Design corpus schema: golden seeds, tool-call templates, structured-output expectations, and stream chunk ordering invariants
Implement deterministic executor: seeding, timeout controls, and replayable request recorder
Add oracle checks: schema conformance, token-ordering checks for streaming, KV-cache continuity checks across partial responses
Integrate with CI: lightweight canary stage that targets dedicated runners and artifacts storage
Build dashboard dashboarding hooks: pass/fail trends, flaky candidate list, and regression heatmap per runtime variant
Document rollout plan and on-call runbook for triaging false positives
